# QA round 2 brief: story ABC-123

Load and follow the `qa-verification` skill for story ABC-123, including its evidence capture and its closing status decision.

## Hand back

- The story's final state.
- The verdict and evidence for each acceptance criterion and each Definition of Done item.
- Any item left outstanding, with its owner.
- Any incidental defect you noted.
- Each PR you merged, with the head SHA its review of record covered.

## Working rules

- Keep working until everything this brief asks for is done, and only stop to ask when you can't go on without the coordinator or before a risky step. Hand back any item left outstanding with its owner.
- Do not start review or hardening rounds, or launch reviewer subagents, beyond the review gates this brief and the skills it tells you to load define.

## Merge rules

A review of record binds only to the exact head it reviewed, so any change to the head, including an update-branch, needs a delta review posted before merging. Every merge must run the merge guard in `references/code-review.md` and carry the reviewed full head SHA as the expected-head condition (`gh pr merge <n> --match-head-commit <full reviewed SHA>`).

## Git rule

Run every commit-creating git command with the git identity already configured and, when `profile.git.signed_commits` is true, the signing already configured. Never pass `-c user.name`, `-c user.email`, `--author`, `GIT_AUTHOR_*` or `GIT_COMMITTER_*`; never write `user.name` or `user.email` with `git config`; and when signing is on never pass `-c user.signingkey`, `-c gpg.*` or `-c commit.gpgsign`. A missing identity, a failed signing check, or a pushed commit whose `.commit.verification.verified` is false is a configuration fault: stop, do not override per command or write git config, make no further commits, and report it.

## Secrets rule

Never write secrets to files or argv.

## Shell rule

Run each shell step as one simple command with literal values. Never assign a variable and use it in the same command; never feed a `$(...)` result into a later argument of the same command; never prefix a command with an inline `VAR="$SECRET"` assignment.
